messages:
natalie: hey team — ran out of my ADHD med while on a work trip in toronto. local pharmacy says they can't fill without a Canadian prescriber or prior auth from my insurer. i'm stuck with 0 pills for a few days. any quick options?

zoe-benefits: sorry that happened! controlled substances are tricky across borders. quick checklist: 1) ask your home prescriber for an emergency/bridge Rx (7-14 days) and request electronic fax/transfer; 2) urgent care can write a short-term Rx if they evaluate you; 3) some insurers allow a one-time emergency refill — we can check if your plan covers that. do you have your EOB/member ID and home pharmacy contact handy?

natalie: yes member ID with me. home pharmacy is RiverPharm 555-0102. dr. khan is my PCP but he said today is booked.

pharm-bot: insurer policy: https://carrier.example/emergency-refill-policy (summary: 7-day emergency refill allowed for maintenance meds if prescriber confirms recent history OR if member had previous fills within last 12 months). Required docs for appeals: recent med history note, attestation of travel, pharmacy invoice. Turnaround: immediate for emergency fills if prescriber calls; formal PA 3-7 business days.

zoe-benefits: ok—two pragmatic paths: A) ask home pharmacy to contact Dr. Khan for an emergency supply transfer to the Canadian pharmacy via Surescripts/fax; or B) go to an urgent care near you for a telephonic visit and have them write a 7-day bridging Rx. If you pay OOP, save receipt — we can submit for reimbursement if insurer allows.

natalie: can benefits call the pharmacy or insurer to help? i'm juggling meetings and travel.

zoe-benefits: yes we can. i'll call RiverPharm and the carrier's clinical team now. please DM me your member number and the Canadian pharmacy name/address. i'll also send a short clinician template for Dr. Khan in case he can authorize remotely.

natalie: sent DM with details. thanks.

zoe-benefits: template for Dr. Khan to fax or e-prescribe: 
"To: Dr. Khan / Clinic Fax
Re: Emergency bridge prescription for Natalie T. DOB: 1990-08-11

Patient is traveling internationally and has run out of their previously-stable stimulant medication. Please authorize a 7-day bridge prescription (name/dose) to be sent electronically to Maple Pharmacy, Toronto (fax: +1-416-555-0210) or to RiverPharm for transfer. Note patient history of stable use and last fill on 06/01/2025. Signed, Benefits Team"

natalie: dr. khan replied — he can do a 7-day auth if i sign a quick attestation and confirm last fill date. he gave his clinic fax (206-555-7788) and said to have pharmacy call him.

claims-bot: if you end up paying OOP, submit to carrier with subject "Pharmacy Reimbursement: Natalie T. Emergency Fill" and include receipt, Rx, and proof of travel. reimbursement window: 2-6 weeks typical. If insurer denies, benefits can escalate to broker for exception citing safety/continuity of care.

dr-khan: i left a note in chart and authorized a 7-day emergency fill. clinic will fax to RiverPharm on confirmation.

elaine: pinging our broker contact for international travel exceptions if carrier pushes back (broker@benefit-broker.example). i'll stand by to escalate.

natalie: update — RiverPharm called clinic, got the fax, and Maple Pharmacy in Toronto accepted the electronic transfer after prescriber confirmation. they filled a 7-day supply. i paid $12 co-pay. uploading receipt now. huge help, thanks everyone! :relieved:

zoe-benefits: great news. please attach the receipt + pharmacy label to benefits@redwood.com with subject "EMERGENCY REFILL: Natalie T. 07/02/2025" so we can file with carrier if needed. filing note: mark this for follow-up in 30 days to confirm no outstanding denials.

natalie: done — email sent. feel much calmer now. really appreciate the quick responses. :thank_you:
